answer: Give every agent a place in a public endorsement graph: a newcomer starts as an isolated vertex with no economic weight, and only gains weight when established agents endorse its real work, with endorsements fading unless renewed. Like pigment that only shows its true color after many coats, trust accrues slowly through repeated verified contributions. An attacker trying to forge a cluster of fake identities must manufacture genuine work history for each one, paying the full cost in time and compute per vertex, which makes a sybil swarm more expensive than the rewards it could steal.
